coverage: Historical chapters, branches, Party offices, prison organizations and affiliated organizing centers, including local National Committee to Combat Fascism (NCCF) groups. Includes every city/locality in the cited 1971 directory, supplemented by Party newspapers, participant accounts and local archives. Some later records concern the Eastern wing after the 1971 split. Neighborhood entries share their city marker; a branch active in several municipalities can have several location markers.

coordinate_source.label: U.S. Census Bureau · 2025 place Gazetteer internal points
coordinate_source.note: Modern approximate place coordinates, not historical street addresses. San Quentin, Algiers and Angola use GeoNames locality coordinates (Angola via Mapcarta).

directory-1971.label: 1971 affiliate directory · printed pages 88–89
directory-1971.note: House Committee on Internal Security, Gun-Barrel Politics (1971). A partial historical directory combining police reports and Party newspaper lists; classifications changed over time.

directory-1970.label: The Black Panther · June 27, 1970, printed page 22
directory-1970.note: The Party newspaper lists recognized chapters, branches, NCCFs and community centers.

howard.label: Elbert “Big Man” Howard · Remembering the Party’s expansion
howard.note: A founding member names additional chapter and branch communities.

washington.label: Seattle Black Panther Party Interpretive Center · Chapter history
washington.note: Identifies branches in Tacoma and Eugene and a prison chapter in Walla Walla.

illinois.label: Illinois Chapter Historical Preservation Society · Operational sites
illinois.note: Documents Illinois branch headquarters, West Suburban Branch localities and Carbondale’s NCCF office.

north-carolina.label: State Library of North Carolina · Black Panther Party
north-carolina.note: Documents Winston-Salem and its High Point community information center; distinguishes unrecognized Charlotte organizing.

algiers.label: UC Berkeley · International Section archive, Algiers
algiers.note: Archival photographs identify members of the Party’s International Section in Algiers.

san-jose-1969.label: The Black Panther · August 9, 1969, printed page 19
san-jose-1969.note: San Jose Liberation School, signed by San Jose Branch members Gregg Wheadon and Judy Graham. The original newspaper is preserved in the NPPC archive.

east-palo-alto.label: East Palo Alto Community Archive · A Structure for Survival, 1972
east-palo-alto.note: Cataloged Party newspaper article documenting the East Palo Alto branch opening in September 1972.

connecticut-thornton.label: Steve Thornton · Remembering Butch Lewis
connecticut-thornton.note: Local history drawing on Thornton’s interview with Hartford Panther Butch Lewis; names Connecticut chapters established by 1969.

connecticut-humanities.label: Connecticut Humanities · The Rise of the Black Panther Party in Connecticut
connecticut-humanities.note: Steve Thornton’s account includes the Waterbury chapter.

right-on-norfolk.label: Right On! · November–December 1972, printed page 4
right-on-norfolk.note: The Eastern wing’s newspaper after the 1971 Party split; identifies Virginia State Chapter leadership organizing in Norfolk.

right-on-louisville.label: Right On! · November–December 1972, printed page 11
right-on-louisville.note: Louisville Express reports Kentucky State Chapter organizing. This is the Eastern wing’s newspaper after the 1971 Party split.

richmond-vcu.label: VCU Libraries · Richmond Panther information center, 1970
richmond-vcu.note: November 25, 1970 film and archival context identifying a community information center at 8 East Baker Street.

tampa-1970.label: FBI memorandum · Tampa NCCF, December 1, 1970
tampa-1970.note: Contemporary report of an operating Tampa NCCF headquarters. Used only as evidence of location and organizational designation.

charleston-1970.label: FBI memorandum · Charleston NCCF, November 27, 1970
charleston-1970.note: The Columbia field office reports an NCCF in Charleston, South Carolina. The field office’s city is not the organizing location.

angola-wallace.label: Herman Wallace · The Angola prison chapter
angola-wallace.note: Participant account of requesting and receiving permission from the Oakland Central Committee to organize a prison chapter.

houston-frost.label: TCU Civil Rights in Black and Brown · Claude Frost oral history
houston-frost.note: The People’s Party II Becomes Part of Black Panther Party, interview recorded June 11, 2016.

southern-history.label: University of Washington · Adam Nolan, Southern Injustice and Radical Discontent
southern-history.note: 2014 history thesis: Louisville’s successful 1972 organization, page 18; Houston’s successive organizations, pages 40–46.
